events.headline: Anthropic picks Google Cloud as preferred provider; TPU/GPU clusters
events.summary: Google Cloud announced that Anthropic selected it as preferred cloud provider, with Google intending to build large-scale next-generation TPU and GPU clusters for Anthropic to train and deploy its AI systems, with no dollar or capacity terms disclosed.

source.title: Anthropic Forges Partnership With Google Cloud to Help Deliver Reliable and Responsible AI

compute.chips: next-generation TPU and GPU clusters (Google to build)

events.notes: Earliest dated Google Cloud compute commitment; release states 'Claude runs on Google Cloud'. No dollar, chip-count or GW figure. The ~$300M Google equity stake reported by the FT at the time is a separate investment event (desk-deals), not in this release.

events.headline: Amazon to invest up to $4B; AWS becomes primary cloud
events.summary: Amazon announced it would invest up to $4B in Anthropic for a minority stake while Anthropic named AWS its primary cloud provider for mission-critical workloads and agreed to use AWS Trainium and Inferentia chips to build, train and deploy future foundation models.

source.title: Amazon and Anthropic announce strategic collaboration to advance generative AI

compute.term: long-term; AWS primary cloud for mission-critical workloads; no compute-spend commitment disclosed

events.notes: 'Up to $4B' is an investment cap, not funded capital and not compute spend. Amazon's Q2-2026 10-Q confirms the money was invested as convertible notes: $8.0B cumulative from Q3 2023 to Q4 2025 (covers this tranche plus Mar 2024 and Nov 2024). This release is the origin of the AWS-primary-cloud and Trainium/Inferentia commitments that Amazon's 10-Q says were later amended (Q2 2026).

events.headline: Google Cloud expands Anthropic partnership; TPU v5e for Claude inference
events.summary: Google announced Anthropic would be among the first to deploy Cloud TPU v5e at scale to serve Claude, alongside one of the industry's largest GKE clusters, AlloyDB, BigQuery and Google security services, with no dollar figure.

source.title: Google announces expansion of AI partnership with Anthropic

compute.chips: Cloud TPU v5e (inference); Multislice training across tens of thousands of interconnected TPU chips

events.notes: Shows Claude serving on TPUs by Nov 2023 (release says 'serve its Claude LLM'), i.e. TPU inference precedes the 2025 1M-TPU deal. Google-stated performance claims (2.3x training, 2.7x serving per dollar vs prior gen) are vendor marketing, not Anthropic cost data.

events.headline: Amazon invests another $4B; AWS named primary training partner
events.summary: Amazon committed an additional $4B (total $8B) and Anthropic named AWS its primary training partner as well as primary cloud provider, agreeing to train and deploy future foundation models on Trainium and Inferentia and to work with Annapurna Labs on future Trainium generations.

source.title: Amazon to invest additional $4 billion in Anthropic

compute.chips: Trainium (training) and Inferentia (deployment); future Trainium generations co-developed with Annapurna Labs
compute.term: AWS primary cloud and training partner; no compute-spend figure disclosed

events.notes: The Amazon page itself carries no date or $8B total (date and total from TechCrunch Nov 22 2024); Amazon's Q2-2026 10-Q independently confirms $8.0B of convertible notes invested Q3 2023-Q4 2025. Investment, not compute spend.

events.headline: AWS unveils Project Rainier Trainium2 cluster for Anthropic
events.summary: At re:Invent AWS announced Trainium2 general availability and Project Rainier, an EC2 UltraCluster of Trn2 UltraServers with hundreds of thousands of Trainium2 chips and more than 5x the exaflops Anthropic used to train its then-current models.

source.title: AWS Trainium2 instances now generally available

compute.chips: Trainium2 (hundreds of thousands) in Project Rainier; Trainium3 (3nm) previewed for late 2025
compute.term: >5x exaflops vs Anthropic's then-current training cluster; no dollar figure

sites: multiple US data centers (Indiana named Oct 2025)

events.notes: Chip count in 2024 is only 'hundreds of thousands'; the ~500,000 live figure is from the Oct 2025 activation. Vendor price-performance claim (30-40% vs GPU instances) is AWS-stated and relevant to Anthropic's Trainium cost advantage thesis but not an Anthropic disclosure.

events.headline: Anthropic to use up to 1M Google TPUs; over 1GW in 2026
events.summary: Anthropic announced it will expand its Google Cloud use to up to one million TPUs, a deal it describes as worth tens of billions of dollars, bringing well over a gigawatt of capacity online in 2026.

source.title: Expanding our use of Google Cloud TPUs and Services

compute.chips: Google TPUs (up to 1,000,000; seventh-generation Ironwood cited by Google)
compute.term: capacity online during 2026; dollar value stated only as 'tens of billions'

events.notes: Dollar figure is undisclosed ('tens of billions'); gw=1.0 is a floor ('well over a gigawatt'); 'up to' 1M TPUs is a ceiling. SiliconANGLE notes 'the companies didn't talk about numbers'. The $10B Broadcom TPU order (Dec 2025) and $35B TPU SPV (Jun 2026) are the first hard dollar figures tied to this TPU supply chain.

events.headline: AWS opens Project Rainier Indiana campus, ~500K Trainium2 chips
events.summary: AWS said Project Rainier is operational with nearly 500,000 Trainium2 chips for Anthropic, expected to exceed one million chips by end-2025, at an Indiana campus SiliconANGLE reports as an $11B build planned to reach more than 2.2 GW across 30 buildings.

source.title: Project Rainier: AWS's Trainium2 compute cluster for Anthropic

compute.term: operational Oct 2025; site planned to reach 30 buildings

sites: St. Joseph County (New Carlisle area), Indiana
other.usd_m_is: AWS site capex, not an Anthropic payment obligation

events.notes: The AWS page is undated in fetch; Oct 29 date from SiliconANGLE/CNBC headlines. '$11B' and '2.2 GW' are AWS site capex and planned capacity reported by SiliconANGLE (T3) - they are not Anthropic contract values and must not be added to Anthropic's commitments. Amazon's Indiana plan was later expanded to $15B (aboutamazon headline Nov 24 2025, seen in RSS only). 'More than 1M Trainium2 chips in use' is confirmed by Anthropic's Apr 20 2026 post.

events.headline: Anthropic commits $50B to US data centers with Fluidstack
events.summary: Anthropic announced a $50B investment in American computing infrastructure, building custom data centers with Fluidstack in Texas and New York with sites coming online throughout 2026 and about 800 permanent and 2,400 construction jobs.

source.title: Anthropic invests $50 billion in American AI infrastructure

compute.term: sites online throughout 2026; Texas and New York, 'more sites to come'

events.notes: $50B is an announced program size ('investment'); the release gives no GW, chip type, financing or lease terms and TechCrunch confirms no capacity figure. Later evidence (Hut 8 River Bend Fluidstack lease with Google backstop; Broadcom/Apollo SPV for 'Fluidstack-based sites') shows the build is financed by developer leases plus TPU SPV notes rather than Anthropic cash capex. Do not add to other Fluidstack-linked rows.

events.headline: Anthropic commits $30B to Azure; up to 1GW Nvidia capacity
events.summary: Anthropic committed to purchase $30B of Azure compute and to contract up to one additional gigawatt on NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems, while NVIDIA committed to invest up to $10B and Microsoft up to $5B in Anthropic.

source.title: Microsoft, NVIDIA and Anthropic announce strategic partnerships

compute.chips: NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems
compute.term: term not disclosed in release; non-cancelable through May 2033 per prospectus coverage (Stocktwits relay, not primary)

events.notes: $30B is 'committed to purchase' (contracted; term unstated); 1 GW is 'up to' ('additional compute capacity up to one gigawatt', 'initially up to one gigawatt'). The $15B of investment is 'up to' and partly inside the Series G (funded amount undisclosed). Circularity: the investors are also the compute vendors. amount_usd_m holds the investment cap only; compute dollars are in compute.usd_m.

events.headline: Broadcom names Anthropic as $10B Google TPU customer
events.summary: On Broadcom's fiscal Q4 call CEO Hock Tan identified Anthropic as the previously unnamed customer that ordered $10B of Google-designed TPUs in the prior quarter and as among the first users of Google's Ironwood TPU.

source.title: Broadcom's stock falls despite another crushing earnings revenue beat

compute.chips: Google TPU incl. Ironwood (racks/systems ordered from Broadcom)
compute.term: order placed in Broadcom fiscal Q3 2025; delivery timing not stated in the opened source

other.unverified_add_on: an additional ~$11B order (total ~$21B) appears in RSS headlines only

events.notes: Trade-press report of the earnings-call disclosure (primary = call transcript, not opened; CNBC 403). $10B is a customer order Broadcom booked, i.e. Anthropic buys TPU systems directly from Broadcom in addition to renting TPU capacity from Google Cloud - a different cost structure (capex-like order) from the Oct 2025 Google Cloud deal. An additional $11B order (total ~$21B) is visible only in RSS headlines (Analytics India, 247wallst) and is NOT used; see open_items.

events.headline: Hut 8 signs $7B River Bend lease with Fluidstack, Google-backed
events.summary: Hut 8 signed a 15-year, 245 MW triple-net lease with Fluidstack at River Bend, Louisiana worth $7.0B over the base term ($17.7B with renewals) with a Google financial backstop, and later described it as part of a partnership with Anthropic and Fluidstack.

source.publisher: SEC EDGAR - Hut 8 Corp. Form 8-K Ex.99.1
source.title: Hut 8 and Fluidstack River Bend lease announcement

corroboration.publisher: SEC EDGAR - Hut 8 Q4-2025 results Ex.99.1 (Anthropic partnership language)
The Decoder (FT investigation: Hut 8 among Google-backed Anthropic sites)

compute.partner: Fluidstack (tenant) at Hut 8 River Bend; Google financial backstop
compute.term: 15-year base term + three 5-year renewals ($17.7B incl. renewals); first data hall Q2 2027

sites: River Bend, Louisiana (330 MW utility capacity; Entergy)
other.backstop: Google (S&P AA+, Moody's Aa2) covers base-term lease payments
other.financing_detail: up to 85% LTC from J.P. Morgan/Goldman Sachs at signing; $3.25B senior secured notes at River Bend by Aug 2026 (Hut 8 Q2 release)

events.notes: The Dec 17 8-K names Fluidstack as tenant and Google as backstop; Anthropic is NOT named in it. The Anthropic link rests on Hut 8's Feb 25 2026 release ('Launched a partnership with Anthropic and Fluidstack') and on the FT's list of Google-backstopped crypto-miner sites (via The Decoder). $7.0B is the lessee's (Fluidstack's) base-term obligation, not an Anthropic payment; Anthropic's own payments flow to Fluidstack under the $50B program (terms undisclosed). Do not add to Anthropic totals without the Fluidstack-Anthropic contract.

events.headline: The Information: Anthropic's 2025 gross margin ~40%, below ~50% plan
events.summary: The Information reported, via TipRanks, that Anthropic's 2025 gross profit margin was about 40%, roughly 10 points below its earlier internal forecast, because inference costs on Google and Amazon cloud ran about 23% above expectations.

source.title: AI Startup Anthropic Warns of Profit Margin Pressure as Costs Surge

extracted.margin_type: gross profit margin CY2025 (The Information; cost scope not specified; earlier internal forecast ~50%)

events.notes: Single-outlet scoop (The Information, Jan 21 2026; original paywalled) read via TipRanks (Jan 22). The 40% is reported, not audited, and the cost scope is undefined (The Information's Nov 2025 note says its gross-margin calculation includes only costs for paying users, per X post seen in search results). TipRanks' 'about $9 billion in the second half' is an annualized run-rate, not recognized revenue (FY2025 revenue ~$4.6B per prospectus coverage). Primary driver is cloud-provider inference pricing - the partner-hosted cost line that the Amazon/Google deals are meant to bend.

events.headline: Anthropic pledges to cover grid upgrades and power price impact
events.summary: Anthropic committed to pay 100% of grid upgrades needed to interconnect its data centers, to bring net-new generation online to match demand and to fund peak-demand curtailment, citing a U.S. AI need of at least 50 GW.

source.title: Covering electricity price increases from our data centers

other.us_ai_capacity_need_gw: at least 50 (over the next several years)
other.jobs: hundreds of permanent and thousands of construction jobs

events.notes: Policy commitment with no dollar figures, sites or capacity. It is a potential unbudgeted cost line for the gross-margin bridge (interconnection upgrades, generation, curtailment) that will sit in data-center/lease pass-through costs rather than chip costs; amount unknown. The 50 GW figure is a U.S. sector estimate, not Anthropic's capacity.

events.headline: The Information: Anthropic to pay Amazon, Google, Microsoft $80B+ through 2029
events.summary: The Information reported Anthropic expects to pay Amazon, Google and Microsoft at least $80B through 2029 to run Claude on their servers, plus revenue-share payouts rising from about $360M in 2025 to $1.9B in 2026 and $6.4B in 2027.

source.title: Anthropic Set to Pay Cloud Partners $80 Billion Through 2029

compute.term: at least $80B through 2029 (forecast of server costs to run Claude; not a contract)

other.revenue_share_pct_of_revenue: roughly one-tenth of projected revenue in those years
other.amazon_gross_profit_share: roughly half of Anthropic's gross profit on sales via Amazon has gone to Amazon

events.notes: This is the source behind the '$80B+' figure: it is 3 partners (not 6), a forecast of hyperscaler server costs through 2029 (from Anthropic's own forecasts per The Information), and pre-dates the Apr-Sep 2026 deal wave. It is superseded by The Information's Dec 2025 investor guidance (~$180B server rental through 2029, via remio.ai) and by the $517B (Sep 6) tally. Revenue-share payouts are a separate line (Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry resale) that sits between gross revenue and net revenue; '$1.3 million' for 2024 is as printed by PYMNTS and looks low versus 2025's $360M - verify against the original.

events.headline: Report: Google nears $5B+ financing for Anthropic Texas data center
events.summary: WinBuzzer, relaying an FT report, says Google is nearing a financing deal of more than $5B for an Anthropic-leased Texas data center developed by Nexus Data Centers, about 500 MW initially and expandable to roughly 7.7 GW.

source.title: Google nears $5 billion financing for Anthropic Texas data center

corroboration.publisher: aiweekly.co (FT Aug 4: Morgan Stanley $15B Texas campus financing under discussion)

compute.chips: Google TPUs ('exclusive rights to supply up to 1 million custom AI chips' per relay)
compute.term: lease signed March 2026 per relay; banks competing to finance initial phase by mid-year; ~7.7 GW expansion potential

other.usd_m_is: Google financing for the initial phase, not an Anthropic payment

events.notes: Low-quality relay of an FT report (FT original not opened; date of the FT piece is ~Mar 27-30 from RSS, the opened relay is Mar 31). Figures (more than $5B, 500 MW, 7.7 GW) are unconfirmed and may overlap with the FT's Aug 4 'Morgan Stanley $15B Texas campus financing under discussion'. Treat as a lead only; not included in totals.

events.headline: Anthropic, Google, Broadcom expand TPU deal; ~3.5GW from 2027
events.summary: Anthropic signed an agreement with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity from 2027, with Broadcom's 8-K stating Anthropic will access about 3.5 GW through Broadcom, consumption dependent on Anthropic's continued commercial success.

source.title: Anthropic expands partnership with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of next-generation compute

compute.term: from 2027; Broadcom-Google Long Term Agreement runs through up to 2031 (separate agreement); no dollar figure in either T1 source

sites: most of the new compute to be sited in the US
other.gw_basis: approximately 3.5 GW through Broadcom, part of 'multiple gigawatts' (Series H T1 says 5 GW Google+Broadcom)

events.notes: Two independent T1 sources (Anthropic, Broadcom 8-K) agree on multi-GW and 2027 start; 3.5 GW is Broadcom's figure. Broadcom says consumption 'is dependent on Anthropic's continued commercial success' (conditional demand). GW overlap: Anthropic's Series H page calls the Google/Broadcom program 'five gigawatts', and TechCrunch's Apr 24 article does not say whether Google's 5 GW is additional to 3.5 GW - we treat 3.5 GW as part of 5 GW (not additive). Dollar value is not disclosed here; the prospectus coverage gives Broadcom-related equipment leases of $161.2B (T3 relay) and Google $111.1B.

events.headline: CoreWeave announces multi-year compute agreement with Anthropic
events.summary: CoreWeave announced a multi-year agreement to support development and deployment of Claude, with a phased roll-out and compute coming online later in 2026, and disclosed no dollar value, chip type or capacity.

source.title: CoreWeave announces multi-year agreement with Anthropic

compute.chips: GPU cloud (models not disclosed in release)
compute.term: multi-year; phased roll-out; capacity online later in 2026

events.notes: Existence and multi-year term are T1 (CoreWeave release and Q1 8-K listing it among Q1 highlights); no value, MW or backlog attribution anywhere (CoreWeave total backlog $99.4B). CoreWeave's Sep 17 convertible-offering deck adds only a one-line 'Anthropic partnership' reference. Not included in dollar totals.

events.headline: Amazon invests $5B, up to $20B more; Anthropic pledges $100B+ to AWS
events.summary: Anthropic and Amazon expanded their collaboration to up to 5 GW of capacity with Amazon investing $5B now and up to $20B more while Anthropic commits more than $100B over ten years to AWS technologies.

source.title: Anthropic and Amazon expand their compute collaboration

compute.chips: Trainium2 and Trainium3 (through Trainium4) plus Graviton; >1M Trainium2 chips already in use
compute.term: 10 years; nearly 1 GW of Trainium2/3 online by end-2026; new Trainium2 capacity in 1H26; Trainium3 later in 2026

sites: inference expansion in Asia and Europe
other.financing_facility_10q: aggregate facility not to exceed $20.0B; nothing drawable at inception; made available as AWS reaches compute-delivery milestones; expires 30 months after an Anthropic liquidity event; draws are new convertible notes (common stock after an IPO, subject to an ownership cap); $15.0B remaining after the $5.0B Series H participation

events.notes: 'More than $100B over ten years' is a floor on Anthropic's AWS spend (contractual obligations under the 'amended commercial arrangement' per Amazon's Q2 10-Q); 5 GW is 'up to'. amount_usd_m=25,000 is $5B invested now plus up to $20B later; the $20B is NOT committed equity: Amazon's 10-Q describes a facility that becomes available only as AWS delivers compute milestones, so a portion of Amazon's 'investment' is effectively vendor financing recycled into AWS spend (circular). Series H counts $5B of Amazon inside the round.

events.headline: Google to invest up to $40B in Anthropic, plus 5GW capacity
events.summary: TechCrunch, citing Bloomberg and Anthropic, reports Google will invest up to $40B in Anthropic ($10B now at a $350B valuation, $30B more on performance targets) alongside 5 GW of Google Cloud capacity over the next five years.

source.title: Google to invest up to $40B in Anthropic in cash and compute

corroboration.publisher: Anthropic (May 6: 'Google: 5 GW agreement ... begin coming online in 2027')
Anthropic Series H page ('Google and Broadcom for five gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity')

compute.term: 5 GW over the next five years; capacity begins coming online in 2027 per Anthropic's May 6 post

other.gw_overlap_note: Series H page names 5 GW for Google+Broadcom combined; Broadcom 8-K names ~3.5 GW through Broadcom as part of the multiple GW - treat as overlapping, not additive

events.notes: Investment amount is 'up to' and conditional ($30B on performance targets); the 5 GW is Google Cloud capacity with no stated dollar value (The Information's May 5 2026 headline says Anthropic committed to spend $200B on Google's cloud and chips - headline only, not opened). Anthropic's own pages confirm a '5 GW' Google/Google-Broadcom agreement but not the $40B figure; TechCrunch attributes the $10B/$30B structure to Anthropic and the headline to Bloomberg.

events.headline: Anthropic takes SpaceX Colossus 1: 300MW, 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs
events.summary: Anthropic announced access to more than 300 MW (over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs) of SpaceX compute within the month, using it to double Claude Code five-hour rate limits and raise Opus API limits, while SEC filings show the agreement was executed May 3 2026 and covers all of Colossus' compute.

source.title: Higher usage limits for Claude and a compute deal with SpaceX

corroboration.publisher: SEC CORRESP 2026-05-20 (SpaceX): agreement dated May 3 2026; 'all of COLOSSUS' compute capacity'

compute.term: capacity available 'within the month' of May 2026; no dollar terms at announcement

other.orbital_interest: Anthropic expressed interest in developing multiple GW of orbital AI compute with SpaceX
other.usage_effect: Claude Code 5-hour limits doubled (Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise); Opus API limits raised

events.notes: Announcement carried no dollars; the price surfaced May 20 via the SpaceX S-1. SEC staff correspondence (T1) dates the cloud services agreement to May 3 2026 and says it lets Anthropic use ALL of COLOSSUS' compute capacity. The announced >300 MW / >220K GPUs is Colossus 1 only; later SEC text (Jun 1 CORRESP, Jun 4 FWP) says the fee covers Colossus AND Colossus II - see the May 20 event for the pricing implications. A direct competitor (xAI/SpaceX) is Anthropic's supplier, which the S-1 flags as redeployable on 90 days' notice.

events.headline: SpaceX S-1: Anthropic pays $1.25B/month through May 2029
events.summary: SpaceX's IPO filing disclosed that Anthropic will pay $1.25B per month for compute across Colossus and Colossus II through May 2029, subject to conditions and terminable by either party on 90 days' notice, with a discounted rate for the first two months.

source.title: Anthropic will pay xAI $1.25 billion per month for compute

corroboration.publisher: SEC CORRESP 2026-06-01 (SpaceX): '$1.25 billion per month ... COLOSSUS AND COLOSSUS II'; 90 days' notice
SEC FWP 2026-06-04 (SpaceX roadshow): '$1.25 B monthly fee ... through May 2029, subject to certain conditions'
TechCrunch (S-1 language repeated on pages F-62, F-96, 13, 146)

compute.chips: NVIDIA GPUs (Colossus II next phase: 400MW+, 220K+ GB300)
compute.term: $1.25B/month through May 2029 subject to certain conditions; either party may terminate on 90 days' notice; reduced rate for first two months

other.derived_unit_price: $15B per year for ~300 MW = $50B per GW-year if Colossus 1 only; ~$7.8 per GPU-hour on 220K GPUs; ~$3.9 per GPU-hour if Colossus II's additional 220K GB300s are included (derived, capacity split not disclosed)

events.notes: $1.25B/month is T1 (SEC CORRESP quoting the S-1; SpaceX roadshow FWP). $45B = 36 x $1.25B is the nominal gross, not a firm commitment: the 90-day mutual termination right makes the firm obligation far smaller (Musk: '180 day lease with 90 day notice mutual cancellation thereafter'). gw=0.3 is Colossus 1's capacity per TechCrunch/Anthropic; the contract language covers Colossus and Colossus II, so the $1.25B buys more than 300 MW - the $/GPU-hour is therefore ambiguous. Anthropic's own prospectus (per Reuters/Stocktwits, Sep 29) shows up to $84.5B with SpaceX through 2029, ~88% above the S-1's $45B - see the Sep 29 event.

events.headline: Musk says SpaceX only committed to 180 days on Colossus
events.summary: Musk said SpaceX had only committed to a 180-day Colossus lease with 90-day mutual cancellation thereafter, contradicting the S-1 language of a monthly fee through May 2029 that TechCrunch found repeated on several pages.

source.title: How long is Anthropic's lease with SpaceX? Opinions vary

compute.term: Musk: 180-day lease with 90-day mutual cancellation thereafter; S-1: monthly fee through May 2029, 90 days' notice

other.musk_quote: a 180 day lease with 90 day notice mutual cancellation thereafter

events.notes: Reuters/FT/Yahoo headlines of May 28 ('six-month lease', 'tweet undermines SpaceX's claims') were seen in RSS only; TechCrunch's account is the opened source. The two positions are reconcilable (nominal term to May 2029 with a 90-day exit, plus Musk's claim of a 180-day initial firm period) - what they imply is that the firm SpaceX commitment is months, not years. Neither xAI nor Anthropic clarified. Key-supplier-is-a-competitor risk for Anthropic's capacity planning.

events.headline: Apollo/Blackstone-led $34.5B Broadcom XPV financing funds Anthropic TPUs
events.summary: Apollo-led funds with Blackstone closed an initial $34.5B-35B financing for Broadcom's AI XPV Platform, in $6B A1, $24B A2 and $4.5B B notes, to fund more than 1 GW of Google TPU systems leased to Anthropic for five years.

source.title: Broadcom, Apollo, Blackstone launch $35 billion AI platform

compute.partner: Google TPU systems via Broadcom AI XPV Platform SPV (Apollo/Blackstone lenders)
compute.chips: Google TPU systems/racks (~1 million TPUs per FT)
compute.term: 5-year lease to Anthropic; funded in ~16 stages over a little more than a year (~$24B by summer 2027)

other.broadcom_support: residual value support on the $30B A tranches; max exposure ~$29B; B tranche unguaranteed
other.platform_scope_gw: >20 GW for frontier labs through 2028 (Anthropic and OpenAI)

events.notes: Four independent outlets agree on structure: $6B A1 + $24B A2 + $4.5B B = $34.5B (Apollo's own headline says 'initial $35 billion capital solution'; the $0.5B gap is unexplained - likely fees/equity, and price talk on Jun 2 was $35.5B with a $25B A2). These are lessor-SPV notes that Broadcom/Google credit-enhance because Anthropic has no credit rating; they are NOT Anthropic-issued bonds, but the 5-year lease payments are Anthropic's obligation (part of the $161.2B 'Broadcom-related equipment leases' in the prospectus coverage). Broadcom IR and Apollo originals were not reachable (503/404). The FT (Aug 4) sizes the broader Google/Broadcom/Apollo/Blackstone/Morgan Stanley structure at ~$200B of interconnected contracts, ~$150B tied to chips for Anthropic, with Google exposed to up to ~$44B.

events.headline: Anthropic signs 12+ non-binding LOIs for direct data-center leases
events.summary: MLQ.ai, citing The Information (Jun 11) and Reuters, reports Anthropic has signed more than a dozen non-binding letters of intent for direct U.S. data-center leases totaling over 1 GW of IT capacity, with Google-backed credit under discussion.

source.title: Anthropic Signs 12+ Letters of Intent for Direct Data Center Leases Totaling Over 1 GW

compute.term: non-binding LOIs; due diligence before binding long-term leases

other.gw_basis: 'over 1 GW' of IT capacity across >12 LOIs
other.credit_support: Alphabet-backed guarantee reported as a way to lower lease risk premium

events.notes: Aggregator summary (T4) of The Information (Jun 11 2026) and Reuters, neither opened; the DCD version (seen only as a search result) also refers to 'more than a dozen letters of intent'. LOIs are non-binding and developers/sites are undisclosed, so nothing here is a commitment. Later binding leases (TeraWulf Jul 6, Riot Aug 10) are consistent with this pipeline converting. Not included in dollar totals; 1 GW shown as a pipeline figure only.
